NE405.question: What are "links" and what are they used for in amateur radio?
NE405.answer_a: They are permanently established radio links, e.g. for networking repeaters or connecting to a HAMNET node.
NE405.answer_b: They are facilities, e.g. at repeaters or digipeaters, that allow connections to be set up via the telephone network.
NE405.answer_c: They are connections between different network protocols, e.g. AX-25 and TCP/IP.
NE405.answer_d: They are a list of links, e.g. to amateur radio websites on HAMNET.

NE404.question: Which transmission methods for digital voice are common in amateur radio?
NE404.answer_b: AM voice, FM voice, SSB voice, Olivia, SSTV
NE404.answer_c: FM voice, RTTY, D-STAR, JS8, Olivia
NE404.answer_d: SSB voice, FT8, DMR, PSK31, SSTV

NE403.question: With certain digital methods of voice transmission (e.g. DMR or TETRA), is it possible to conduct several voice contacts simultaneously on the same frequency within one reception area?
NE403.answer_a: Yes. The voice data are transmitted alternately in short, periodic time slots.
NE403.answer_b: Yes. The transmit power is increased to improve the digital error correction.
NE403.answer_c: No. Digital transmissions taking place at the same time inherently interfere with each other.
NE403.answer_d: No. Voice transmissions cannot be split into data packets.

NE402.question: You want to take part in a net using digital voice (e.g. C4FM, DMR or D-Star) via a repeater network. Apart from choosing the transmission method, the frequency and the modulation, what must you pay attention to?
NE402.answer_a: You must select suitable parameters, e.g. reflector, time slot or colour code.
NE402.answer_b: You must use the same firmware version as the repeater network.
NE402.answer_c: All stations must set the same station identifier, e.g. DMR ID.
NE402.answer_d: All stations must be within radio range of the same repeater.

NE401.question: What should you bear in mind when transmitting a text by radioteletype?
NE401.answer_a: The transmitting and receiving stations must use the same transmission method (e.g. JS8, PSK, RTTY) and, where applicable, the same method parameters.
NE401.answer_b: The transmitting and receiving stations must have the same time zone setting (e.g. summer time) for the transmission to succeed.
NE401.answer_c: The transmission should preferably take place in the evening and night-time hours, because the frequencies are kept free for voice contacts during the day.
NE401.answer_d: The transmission should preferably use a fast method, so that the amateur bands are not loaded unnecessarily.

NF118.question: What is meant by a digipeater?
NF118.answer_a: A radio station that automatically retransmits received data packets or parts of them, possibly also with a time delay or repeatedly. Individual data fields may be changed in the process.
NF118.answer_b: A linear transponder that converts received data packets to another frequency band. The mode used and the content of the packet are preserved in the process.
NF118.answer_c: An integrated circuit that prepares digital signals for modulation in the radio. The station's call sign is regularly inserted into the data stream in the process.
NF118.answer_d: A repeater station that retransmits voice transmissions on another frequency. The volume is adjusted adaptively by digital signal processing in the process.

NF117.question: What undesirable effect can occur when a radio is controlled by a computer?
NF117.answer_a: The radio could unexpectedly switch to transmit and thus cause unwanted emissions or endanger people.
NF117.answer_b: The preamplifier is out of action, which could cause interference to adjacent channels and to frequencies in other bands.
NF117.answer_c: The automatic level control (ALC) could be triggered and interfere with other digital equipment.
NF117.answer_d: The computer can act like an electrolytic capacitor in the antenna circuit and thus shift the transmit frequency.

NF116.question: Some transceivers have a so-called CAT interface. This connection is used ...
NF116.answer_a: to control the transceiver, e.g. from a computer, or to query values such as frequency, transmit power or PTT by means of a serial communication protocol.
NF116.answer_b: to tap off or feed in an AF signal (e.g. for DV or POCSAG) with as little distortion as possible by bypassing amplifier and filter stages.
NF116.answer_c: to pass the received RF signal, as unfiltered as possible, to a computer for further processing by digital signal processing.
NF116.answer_d: to connect a rotary encoder or a potentiometer for precise frequency setting without any further circuitry.

NF115.question: Some FM transceivers have an analogue data port (e.g. labelled DATA or called a 9600 port). Its main purpose is ...
NF115.answer_a: to tap off or feed in an AF signal (e.g. for DV or POCSAG) with as little distortion as possible by bypassing amplifier and filter stages.
NF115.answer_b: to control the transceiver, e.g. from a computer, and to query values such as frequency, transmit power or PTT by means of a serial communication protocol.
NF115.answer_c: to pass the received RF signal, as unfiltered as possible, to a computer and process it further by digital signal processing.
NF115.answer_d: to connect a rotary encoder or a potentiometer for precise frequency setting without any further circuitry.

NF114.question: How can a connection be made between a radio and a computer for digital transmission methods (e.g. FT8 or WSPR)?
NF114.answer_a: An audio connection (AF signal, or digital, e.g. via a USB cable) is made between computer and radio, or a hardware modem is used.
NF114.answer_b: The ALC socket of the radio is connected to audio or data ports of the computer by means of a hardware modem.
NF114.answer_c: A software modem is installed and the ALC socket of the radio is connected directly to the computer (possibly via an adapter).
NF114.answer_d: The RF connector (e.g. antenna output) of the radio is connected to a suitable data interface of the computer by means of a Y cable.

NF113.question: Why are the uplink and downlink in satellite operation usually not in the same frequency band? Different frequency bands are used because ...
NF113.answer_a: this makes it easier to separate the transmitted and received signals and reduces the size of the filters on the satellite.
NF113.answer_b: the uplink is attenuated more by the ionosphere than the downlink.
NF113.answer_c: the bandwidth is divided between both frequency bands and the band segments can be used more efficiently.

NF112.question: During an SSB QSO on the 2 m band, the other station reports: "You are not transmitting exactly on my frequency". What could be the cause?
NF112.answer_d: The CW filter is switched on.

NF107.question: Why should a transmitter never be operated without a matched antenna or a dummy load?
NF107.answer_a: The reflected wave could damage the transmitter output stage.
NF107.answer_b: Because the load is missing, the supply voltage is regulated upwards, which can lead to overvoltages.
NF107.answer_c: The absorbed power can overload the transmitter's power supply.
NF107.answer_d: The SWR meter could be damaged.

NF106.question: The diagram shows the display of a transceiver. What is shown in the waterfall display, and how is it shown?
NF106.answer_a: Frequency and time on the axes, and signal strength as colour and/or brightness.
NF106.answer_b: Frequency and signal strength on the axes, and time as colour and/or brightness.
NF106.answer_c: Signal strength and time on the axes, and frequency as colour and/or brightness.
NF106.answer_d: Signal strength and phase on the axes, and time as colour and/or brightness.

AF119.question: A double-conversion superhet has a first IF of 10.7 MHz and a second IF of 460 kHz. The receive frequency is to be 28 MHz. What frequencies are required for the VFO and the CO if the oscillators are to operate above the mixer input signals?
AF119.answer_a: The VFO must oscillate at 38.70 MHz and the CO at 11.16 MHz.
AF119.answer_b: The VFO must oscillate at 10.24 MHz and the CO at 17.30 MHz.
AF119.answer_c: The VFO must oscillate at 17.3 MHz and the CO at 10.24 MHz.
AF119.answer_d: The VFO must oscillate at 28.460 MHz and the CO at 39.16 MHz.

AF118.question: A double-conversion superhet has a first IF of 9 MHz and a second IF of 460 kHz. The receive frequency is to be 21.1 MHz. What frequencies are required for the VFO and the CO if the VFO is to operate above and the CO below the respective mixer input signal?
AF118.answer_a: The VFO must oscillate at 30.1 MHz and the CO at 8.54 MHz.
AF118.answer_b: The VFO must oscillate at 12.1 MHz and the CO at 9.46 MHz.
AF118.answer_c: The VFO must oscillate at 12.1 MHz and the CO at 8.54 MHz.
AF118.answer_d: The VFO must oscillate at 30.1 MHz and the CO at 9.46 MHz.

AF117.question: The following circuit represents a double-conversion superhet. What is the function of the three blocks marked X, Y and Z?
AF117.answer_a: X is a VFO, Y is a CO and Z is a BFO.
AF117.answer_b: X is a VFO, Y is a BFO and Z is a CO.
AF117.answer_c: X is a BFO, Y is a CO and Z is a VFO.
AF117.answer_d: X is a BFO, Y is a VFO and Z is a CO.

AF116.question: What should the bandwidth of the filter for the 1st IF in a double-conversion superhet be?
AF116.answer_a: At least as large as the largest bandwidth required by the intended modes.
AF116.answer_b: At least as large as twice the bandwidth of the mode in use.
AF116.answer_c: At least as large as the widest amateur band to be received.
AF116.answer_d: It must cover the full tuning range of the receiver.

AF115.question: What determines the close-in selectivity of a superhet receiver?
AF115.answer_b: The band-pass filter at the receive frequency

AF114.question: Which relationship between the intermediate frequencies is advantageous for an HF double-conversion superhet?
AF114.answer_a: The 1st IF is higher than twice the maximum receive frequency. After filtering in the roofing filter (1st IF), the signal is mixed down to a lower 2nd IF.
AF114.answer_b: The 1st IF is lower than the maximum receive frequency. After filtering in the roofing filter (1st IF), the signal is mixed up to a higher 2nd IF.
AF114.answer_c: The 1st IF is below the lowest receive frequency. The 2nd IF is above the highest receive frequency.
AF114.answer_d: The 1st IF may be at most half the highest receive frequency. The 2nd IF is higher than twice the lowest receive frequency.

AF113.question: Which statement is correct for a double-conversion superhet?
AF113.answer_a: With a low second IF, good selectivity is easily achieved.
AF113.answer_b: With a low first IF, good cross-modulation performance is easily achieved.
AF113.answer_c: With a high first IF, high sensitivity is easily achieved.
AF113.answer_d: With a low second IF, good image rejection is easily achieved.

AF112.question: Which statement is correct for a double-conversion superhet?
AF112.answer_a: With a high first IF, good image rejection is easily achieved.
AF112.answer_b: The signal picked up by the antenna keeps its frequency all the way to the demodulator.
AF112.answer_c: With a low first IF, good image rejection is easily achieved.
AF112.answer_d: With a low second IF, good image rejection is easily achieved.

AF111.question: What advantage does a high first intermediate frequency offer in superheterodyne receivers?
AF111.answer_b: It reduces the influence of received signals on the local oscillator.

AF110.question: In a superheterodyne receiver with one IF, what mainly determines the image rejection?
AF110.answer_c: The bandwidth of the IF filters

AF109.question: What is the advantage of HF receivers with a very high first IF (e.g. 50 MHz)?
AF109.answer_a: The image frequency lies very far outside the receive range.
AF109.answer_b: Filters for 50 MHz have better selectivity than filters at a lower frequency.
AF109.answer_c: Such a receiver has better strong-signal performance.
AF109.answer_d: You get a receiver for HF and VHF at the same time.

AF106.question: In a single-conversion superhet, what is always the frequency difference between the receive frequency and the image frequency?
AF106.answer_b: The frequency of the local oscillator

AF231.question: The LNB of a satellite receiving system can operate with two different operating voltages. What happens when the supply voltage at the bias tee in the block diagram shown is increased to 18 V?
AF231.answer_b: The LNB switches to another satellite.
AF231.answer_c: The LNB is damaged by overvoltage.
AF231.answer_d: The LNB switches the receive range.

AF230.question: You are receiving the signal of a satellite at 10 GHz. The cable between the LNB and the receiver is 20 m long. Why is the cable loss rather negligible despite the high receive frequency?
AF230.answer_a: The LNB amplifies the received signal and mixes it down to a lower frequency, at which the cable loss is lower.
AF230.answer_b: The remote supply voltage that powers the LNB reduces the cable loss.
AF230.answer_c: Mixing the received signal with the TCXO frequency means that only the baseband is transmitted.
AF230.answer_d: The LNB demodulates the signal. The resulting AF is insensitive to cable loss.

AF229.question: What does a noise factor F = 2 mean for a UHF preamplifier?
AF229.answer_a: The output signal of the amplifier has a signal-to-noise ratio 3 dB lower than that of the input signal.
AF229.answer_b: The output signal of the amplifier has a signal-to-noise ratio 3 dB higher than that of the input signal.
AF229.answer_c: The output signal of the amplifier has a signal-to-noise ratio 6 dB lower than that of the input signal.
AF229.answer_d: The output signal of the amplifier has a signal-to-noise ratio 6 dB higher than that of the input signal.

AF228.question: What does a noise figure of 1.8 dB mean for a UHF preamplifier?
AF228.answer_a: The output signal of the preamplifier has a signal-to-noise ratio 1.8 dB lower than that of the input signal.
AF228.answer_b: The output signal of the preamplifier has a signal-to-noise ratio 1.8 dB higher than that of the input signal.
AF228.answer_c: The noise of the output signal is 1.8 dB lower than the noise of the input signal.
AF228.answer_d: The gain for the wanted signal is 1.8 dB; the noise power remains unchanged.

AF227.question: What is meant by the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of a receiver?
AF227.answer_a: It states by what ratio the wanted signal is stronger than the noise signal.
AF227.answer_b: It states by what ratio the noise signal is stronger than the wanted signal.
AF227.answer_c: It is the frequency spacing between the received signal and the interfering signal.
AF227.answer_d: It is the spacing between the receive frequency and the image frequency.

AF226.question: What is the function of the limiting amplifier in an FM receiver?
AF226.answer_a: Above a certain input signal level, it limits the output signal in order to suppress AM interference.
AF226.answer_b: It reduces the noise of the input stage.
AF226.answer_c: It limits the deviation for the FM demodulator.
AF226.answer_d: It provides complete suppression of the IF carrier in order to avoid AM interference.

AF225.question: Which signals usually control the receiver muting (squelch)?
AF225.answer_b: The RF signal of the input stage.

AF224.question: What does the AGC (automatic gain control) do when the input signal is strong?
AF224.answer_a: It reduces the gain of amplifier stages in the receive section.
AF224.answer_b: It reduces the amplitude of the VFO.
AF224.answer_c: It reduces the amplitude of the BFO.
AF224.answer_d: It increases the gain of amplifier stages in the receive section.
